questions.q: Why are repeat guests so valuable for restaurants?
questions.a: Repeat guests are the biggest driver of restaurant revenue growth. Keeping a guest costs much less than winning a new one, and existing guests tend to spend more per order and try new menu items. They're also more likely to recommend you through reviews and referrals.

questions.q: How does customer satisfaction affect repeat visits?
questions.a: Higher satisfaction leads to higher return rates, and more returns lead to more revenue per location. Momos data from operators of every size shows this pattern across large enterprises, mid-sized chains and small operators. The gains are often largest at underperforming locations.

questions.q: How can AI help a restaurant get more repeat guests?
questions.a: AI can predict which guests are likely to return and which locations are at risk, using order history, review sentiment and survey data. It brings feedback from reviews, in-store surveys and delivery apps into one dashboard. It also speeds up replies and recovery and helps teams keep service consistent at peak times.

questions.q: Which metrics should restaurants track to improve guest retention?
questions.a: Track customer satisfaction, repeat-visit rate and response time across all your channels. Together they show whether guests are happy, whether they come back and how quickly you act when something goes wrong. Measuring them consistently helps you see what's working and prove the return on your guest experience work.

questions.q: Is it better to focus on new customers or existing guests?
questions.a: Both matter, but the bigger long-term opportunity usually lies with the guests you already have. Existing guests are more profitable, more loyal and more likely to become advocates. Personal touches like birthday rewards or recommendations based on past orders help turn occasional diners into regulars.
